description: The bar chart illustrates the negative log-probability of clinically relevant tokens for the Mistral-v0.2 model, comparing its baseline performance (blue bars) with versions fine-tuned on data from five different medical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, and Pediatrics. The x-axis displays the specialty terms, with each category containing five bars representing the model's performance on tokens associated with that specialty, with each color corresponding to a different fine-tuning dataset. The y-axis measures the negative log-probability, ranging from approximately -22 to -27, where lower values indicate higher confidence in the model's predictions. For each specialty, the baseline model (blue) generally exhibits a higher negative log-probability (lower confidence) compared to the fine-tuned versions, with the exception of the "Neuro" category, where the fine-tuned model shows a slightly higher negative log-probability than the baseline. Within each specialty group, the fine-tuned models show varying degrees of improvement, with the "Cardio" fine-tuned model (light orange) showing the most significant reduction in negative log-probability, indicating a substantial increase in confidence for Cardio-related tokens. The chart demonstrates that fine-tuning the model on specialty-specific data generally improves its performance on tokens related to that specialty, with the most notable improvements observed in the Cardio and Gastro specialties.
